title: speculative-acceptance: KV coalescer holdback and alt-path decision curve
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: we see bursty fallback behavior in medium-length generative workloads where small timing variance in KV cache arrival and batching causes the serving runtime to flip into a conservative (alt-path) execution for a subset of requests, increasing tail latency and token-cost. Motivation: reduce unnecessary conservative fallbacks while preserving deterministic correctness for edge hardware-model combinations. This PR introduces a speculative-acceptance decision curve plus a KV coalescer holdback window: the runtime will tentatively accept speculative fast-exec decisions based on an adaptive confidence score; if downstream verifies a mismatch, requests are routed to the alt-path and a lightweight reconciliation is triggered. Design summary: 1) speculative acceptance module computes a confidence score from recent kernel success rates, sequence-length distribution, and observed KV arrival jitter. 2) KV coalescer holds short-lived writes (configurable, default 2ms) to give batching a chance without blocking correctness checks. 3) Numeric-mode guard (formerly "precision toggle" concept) exposes an explicit safe-mode flag that forces full-precision execution; otherwise speculative acceptance may opt for quant-mode kernels when confidence is high. 4) Metrics hooks record decisions, verified-mismatch counts, and reconciliation cost for offline tuning. Implementation notes: new modules added under runtime/scheduler (speculative_acceptance.rs) and runtime/kv (coalescer.rs, holdback_policy.rs). Small changes to quant dispatcher to surface the numeric-mode guard and ensure the reconciliation path replays a request with KV cache snapshot. Tests & validation: added deterministic unit tests for acceptance curve edge cases, integration tests that simulate KV jitter and ensure no silent correctness regression, and new loadtest scenarios that measured 18% reduction in fallback frequency on our medium-seq C4 workload with overall median latency impact under 1.5%. Rollout plan: staged rollout using A/B gating in Dedicated; feature gated behind runtime.experimental.speculative_acceptance with an initial 10% canary, monitor verified-mismatch, token-cost and p99 latency for 48 hours, then increment. Rollback: flip feature flag off; reconciliation path is synchronous-safe so turning off speculative acceptance guarantees identical behavior to pre-PR. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf microbench harness - [x] observability dashboards and alerts - [x] docs update for ops (fallback behavior page).

release_notes: Introduces speculative acceptance decision curve and KV coalescer holdback to reduce unnecessary conservative fallbacks. Default is off behind runtime.experimental.speculative_acceptance. Expected impact: ~18% fewer fallbacks on medium sequence workloads; p99 latency unchanged for most workloads. Ops: new observability dashboard and reconciliation cost alert added.
